# sciencedb

The goal of **sciencedb** is to provide a user-friendly, programmatic R
interface to [ScienceDB](https://www.scidb.cn/) (Science Data Bank), a
global generalist data repository managed by the Computer Network
Information Center (CNIC) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). As a
core platform for publishing, sharing, and accessing scientific data
from China and around the world, ScienceDB holds vast, high-value
datasets spanning multidisciplinary research domains.

`sciencedb` bridges this ecosystem with R workflow by allowing users to
search across up to 10,000 datasets by keywords, inspect dataset
metadata, and batch-downloads files directly into their local
environment with smart file management.

## Installation

You can install the development version of sciencedb from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r

# Recommended (fast installer)
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("jennyyzxu/sciencedb")
```

## Example

Below is a basic example demonstrating how an R user can aery multi-word
topics, evaluate dataset structure, and download data files locally:

``` r

library(sciencedb)
```

1.  **Search for Datasets**

    Use [`sdb_search()`](reference/sdb_search.md) to discover datasets
    using keywords. Because queries return deep multi-column metadata,
    fetching queries across thousands of records can take 15 to 30
    seconds depending on network latency. The function returns a cleaned
    data frame where each row represents a dataset and includes 12
    metadata attributes:

    | **Column** | **Description** |
    |----|----|
    | `Title` | Primary English dataset title (falls back to Chinese title if English is absent) |
    | `Author` | Semicolon-separated list of author names |
    | `Keyword` | Semicolon-separated domain keywords |
    | `Publish` | Official dataset release date |
    | `Doi` | Digital Object Identifier associated with the dataset |
    | `Taxonomy` | Scientific classification and subject taxonomy |
    | `Language` | Primary dataset language code (`en`, `zh`, etc.) |
    | `Introduction` | Full dataset abstract and methodological description |
    | `Access` | Rights/conditions (`PUBLIC`, `RESTRICTED`, or `EMBARGO`) |
    | `Views` | Historical platform page view counts |
    | `Downloads` | Total file download metric |
    | `Cstr` | China Science and Technology Resource identifier |

``` r

# Search for datasets related to attachment
results <- sdb_search(keyword = "attachment")

# Preview core metadata columns 
head(results)

Specifically, respondents were asked to answer questions online by scanning the QR code of the questionnaire or clicking on the questionnaire link to open the online evaluation page. In order to ensure the quality of the survey data, we appointed corresponding instructors and suggested that they do a good job in organizing the questionnaire test, such as suggesting that they conduct a centralized assessment and do not forward the QR code or link to students at will; at the same time, it is recommended that they explain the questionnaire and test instructions to students before the unified test. In the end, a total of 400 subjects participated in the survey, and 52 invalid data were deleted (there are two deletion criteria for invalid questionnaires: First, at least three of the four serious answer questions set in the questionnaire were answered incorrectly; Second, the response time of the questionnaire is obviously too long and too short), and finally 348 valid data were obtained.&nbsp;A data file is included. 2.  **Inspect Dataset Details**

    Once a dataset or DOI of inerest is identified from the search
    results, use [`sdb_dive()`](reference/sdb_dive.md) to pull full file
    lists, directory hierarchies, and version details:

``` r

# Retreive full metadata and file information for a specific dataset
info <- sdb_dive(doi = "10.57760/sciencedb.o00115.00098")

# Preview dataset-relevant research paper
info[[1]]$papers
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$titleZh
#> [1] "Attachment Style and Attention Bias to Emotional Information: The Moderating Effect of Stress, Stimulus Characteristics, and Attention Stage"
#> 
#> [[1]]$titleEn
#> [1] "Attachment Style and Attention Bias to Emotional Information: The Moderating Effect of Stress, Stimulus Characteristics, and Attention Stage"
#> 
#> [[1]]$doi
#> [1] "10.1111/jopy.12891"
#> 
#> [[1]]$url
#> [1] ""
#> 
#> [[1]]$citationFlag
#> NULL
#> 
#> [[1]]$citationZh
#> [1] ""
#> 
#> [[1]]$citationEn
#> [1] ""
#> 
#> [[1]]$state
#> [1] "published"
#> 
#> [[1]]$manuscriptNo
#> [1] ""
#> 
#> [[1]]$journalZh
#> [1] "Journal of Personality"
#> 
#> [[1]]$journalEn
#> [1] "Journal of Personality"
#> 
#> [[1]]$journalCode
#> [1] "o00115"
#> 
#> [[1]]$authors
#> NULL
#> 
#> [[1]]$volume
#> NULL
```

3.  **Download Files**

    Use [`sdb_download()`](reference/sdb_download.md) to download
    dataset files to your local directory. The function automatically
    rename files (e.g., data(1).csv) if duplicates exist:

``` r

# Download all files into a local folder
sdb_download(
  doi = "10.57760/sciencedb.o00115.00098",
  user_path = "~/Desktop"
)
#> Found 3 file(s) to download.
#> [1/3] Downloading: meta-analysis_av.cma ...
#> [2/3] Downloading: meta-analysis_ax.cma ...
#> [3/3] Downloading: power calculation.R ...
#> All downloads completed successfully!
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`sdb_dive()`](sdb_dive.md) : Retrieve Rich Raw Metadata for a
  ScienceDB Dataset
- [`sdb_download()`](sdb_download.md) : Download All Dataset Files to
  Local Directory by DOI
- [`sdb_search()`](sdb_search.md) : Search ScienceDB Datasets by Keyword
